scope: First real-660 forward test of the repair-shadow-motion-lag skill
summary: The first motion-aligned temporal-alpha implementation was rejected: it aligned 313 frames and preserved protected/outside-safety pixels, but the hard displacement threshold increased temporal jerk beyond the accepted parent and failed the full-frame jerk gate.
evidence: The candidate decodes 660/660 frames and reports motion_aligned_frames=313 with a maximum camera-frame shift of 29.9947 pixels.
Protected content and pixels outside the safety mask are exact in every preencode frame.
ROI jerk mean increased from the v71 parent's 1.6804897 to 1.8630811 (ratio 1.10865), failing the skill's 1.03 non-regression gate.
Full-frame jerk mean reached 0.7904145 versus raw 0.6975300 and failed the renderer's 1.12 bound.
The independent assessment is saved as motion-lag-assessment.json and remains PARTIAL with human review unset.
lessons: Switching an entire translated alpha field on at a fixed motion threshold creates second-order discontinuities near the threshold.
High-confidence skin/arm cleanup alpha must not be spatially migrated with the low-alpha shadow band.
Camera-frame arm centroids need temporal denoising before they drive alpha warping.
limitations: This candidate is not accepted and must not replace v71 or be used as the lightening parent.
The automatic clean-plate proxy cannot establish perceptual shadow attachment without dense human review.
next_actions: Use median-filtered centroids, a continuous displacement confidence ramp, and low-alpha-only motion warping.
Rerun the complete 660-frame non-regression gates in a new immutable directory.
